name: Maryland

notes: Food for home consumption is exempt; soft drinks and candy are taxed at 6%, which is not counted here.
Alcoholic beverages are taxed at 9%, bought in stores or served.
Drinks served are taxed at 9%, like bottles bought in stores.

Cigarettes are taxed at 6%, on top of the $5.00-a-pack excise (since July 1, 2024), left out here; most other tobacco carries a 60% wholesale excise (premium cigars 15%); vaping devices and liquid in containers over 5 ml pay a 20% sales tax, and liquid in smaller containers 60%, which isn't counted here: it falls only on vapor products, and no official figure gives their share of tobacco sales.
Household supplies: diapers and baby wipes have been exempt since July 1, 2022, which is not taken out here.
Personal care products: tampons, sanitary pads and other menstrual products are exempt, which is not taken out here.
Barber and beauty services aren't taxed: Maryland taxes only the services its law lists (not re-verified with the Comptroller).
Clothing is taxed. The Shop Maryland Tax-Free Week (August 9 to 15, 2026) exempted clothing and footwear of $100 or less an item and the first $40 of a backpack, which is not taken out here.
Laundry and dry cleaning for households aren't taxed (not re-verified with the Comptroller).
Home furnishings: the Shop Maryland Energy weekend (February 14 to 16, 2026) exempted Energy Star appliances, which is not taken out here.
Motor fuel is exempt from the sales tax and taxed by the gallon instead: 46.6 cents for gasoline from July 1, 2026, left out here.
Auto repair labor: car repair labor isn't taxed when stated separately (not re-verified with the Comptroller).
Worcester County levies a 0.5% food and beverage tax in Ocean City (to repay its convention center bonds), counted in Ocean City's restaurant rate.
Hotel stays pay county and city hotel taxes, which are not counted here.
gaps: Maryland has no local sales tax (Ocean City's 0.5% food and beverage tax on restaurant meals aside); the 6% general rate applies everywhere.
Alcoholic beverages, short-term vehicle rentals and some services carry other state rates; the alcohol rate is applied to that category, and the others are not part of these categories.

programs: Sustainable Communities are mapped from the state's layer, whose expiration dates aren't updated on renewal: the 24 past their date are kept because the Department of Housing and Community Development's list of approved communities still names them (October 2026); Millington and Sudlersville are on the list but not on the map. New Market's Main Street isn't on the Main Street layer. Three enterprise zones (Queen Anne's County, Crisfield and Somerset County, and Berlin) are set to expire on December 14, 2026. Business districts are mapped for Baltimore (the Department of Finance's special benefits districts: the Downtown and Waterfront management districts, the York Corridor Business Improvement District and the community benefits districts) and Montgomery County's urban districts. The South Baltimore Gateway Community Impact District, on the same city layer, isn't shown: it is funded by the casino's local impact grants, not by a charge on property.

warn.text: Annapolis draws many visitors, but it isn't flagged as a visitor economy over the city as a whole: {visitor_why}. Visitors' spending is part of its local sales, so its retention rates likely overstate how much of residents' own spending stays local.

Baltimore draws many visitors, most of all to the Inner Harbor, but it isn't flagged as a visitor economy: {visitor_why}. Visitors' spending is part of its local sales, so its retention rates likely overstate how much of residents' own spending stays local, most of all downtown.
